learning: Baseline (iteration 0) failed with off_track at 10-15% progress and 1-2 line losses. Hypothesis: the narrow array and 5 cm lead cause the losses; the wider array and 4 cm lead should reduce them. Check line_loss_events, progress and max_error on all three development tracks, then tune kp if oscillation rises.
notes: Runnable package for the Builder's widened 5-sensor array at 4 cm lead, 0.6 kg. kp raised to 3.0 and kd to 0.1 to compensate for the wider array and the lighter chassis. Full measurement set requested.
rationale: The only race evidence is the iteration-0 baseline (entityR2B, 60 trials, no finishes). Every run ended off_track at 10-15% progress, with 1-2 line-loss events per run and max_error of 0.061-0.065 m against a 0.0625 m limit. Oscillation was low (0.07-0.15), so jitter is not the main failure. The 4 cm array and 5 cm lead lose the tape on bends and the robot drifts out before recovering. I therefore keep the Builder's proposed geometry (five sensors at x = -0.03 to +0.03 m, 1.5 cm pitch, y = 0.04 m, 12 mm footprint, 0.6 kg, 0.11 m track, 0.03 m wheel radius). For the controller, a wider array means the same weight pattern saturates later, so I raise kp from 2.5 to 3.0 to keep correction authority on the bends, and add kd 0.1 to damp the faster response of the lighter chassis. The weights stay [-2,-1,0,1,2], matching the array's left-positive ordering. base_speed stays at 1.6 because progress, not speed, limits the baseline; ki stays at 0 to avoid windup on the curved course. line_loss stays 'last_direction', since the tape still leaves the array on the sharpest bends. Expected result, not measured: line_loss_events falls toward 0 and progress rises above 0.15. The first race will show whether the remaining failure is the forward offset or the gains.
